findings.text: Two globally visible vmstat helpers exist for quieting and draining deferred stat work. One can be called to fold the current CPU diffs when deferred work is pending, the other flushes the dedicated memory percpu workqueue. Both are entry points for other subsystems needing timely global counters.

A global percpu workqueue pointer backs all delayed vmstat maintenance, created during early memory init. The early init routine also wires hotplug handlers, node CPU state, shepherd timing, proc seq views and vm sysctls when the corresponding options are enabled.

Working set tracking exposes a global shadow node reclaim list, an activation hook for folios, and a node membership updater for radix tree nodes. The activation hook is callable from reclaim or access paths, while the updater keeps shadow only nodes discoverable for shrinking.

Mixed block reporting is entirely optional and inert unless page owner tracking is compiled in and initialized. When active it ensures per CPU pages are drained and a per migration type header is emitted before delegating to a node zone walk with a per zone printer.

The pagetype overview show callback skips nodes without memory and otherwise reports block order and pages per block followed by three sections for free lists, block counts and mixed counts. It serves as the show method for the restricted pagetype seq view.

Six seq operation tables share a common node iteration triple while varying only their show callback. Fragmentation, pagetype, zone, unusable and extfrag views reuse the same start next stop helpers, whereas the vmstat table uses its own snapshot based iterator with matching stop cleanup.

Zone detail output distinguishes the first populated zone in a node to attach node wide counters once, scaling huge page aware items. Every zone then reports free pages, boost and watermark levels, span and management counts, low memory reserves, per zone counters, optional NUMA events, per CPU pageset tuning, and reclaim hopelessness with high atomic reserves.
The zoneinfo show callback walks all zones in the supplied node and delegates formatting to a shared printer, without itself filtering memoryless nodes.

Global vmstat iteration snapshots all counter families into one allocation sized by the sum of zone, NUMA, node and generic items plus optional event counters. Collection folds NUMA events, gathers zone and node states with huge page normalization, fills dirty limits and memmap totals, normalizes block IO sectors to kilobytes, and appends a zero valued legacy unstable entry at the end. Iteration is positional with bounds checks and private buffer cleanup.

The stat refresh handler forces a synchronous per CPU fold across all CPUs and then audits global zone and node atomics for unexpected negativity, skipping a small allowlist of counters known to dip below zero. Read handling reports no data while write handling advances the file position by the written length.

Per CPU vmstat maintenance is self perpetuating: a delayed work item folds local diffs and only requeues itself with a rounded interval when that fold observed activity. Idle CPUs therefore stop scheduling until the shepherd rediscovers pending diffs.

Pending work detection scans every populated zone CPU stat diff area for any nonzero byte and, once per node, the corresponding node stat diff area. Any nonzero byte indicates a fold is required; all zero means the CPU is clean.

Quieting is a best effort fast path that does nothing before the system is running, when no delayed work is pending, or when no diffs exist. Otherwise it performs an immediate local fold without cancelling the pending delayed item, leaving periodic cleanup to the shepherd.

A periodic shepherd protects CPU hotplug with a read lock, visits each online CPU, skips isolated CPUs under RCU protection, and queues immediate work only for idle workers that have pending diffs, yielding periodically. It always requeues itself on a rounded interval, while early startup initializes deferrable per CPU work and disables items for CPUs that are not yet online.

CPU arrival refreshes stat thresholds, marks the CPU node as having CPUs, and enables that CPU delayed work. Preparation for removal synchronously disables the work item, while the dead handler refreshes thresholds again and clears the node CPU state only when the node has no remaining CPUs.

Early memory internal setup creates a reclaim capable percpu workqueue, registers dead and online hotplug states with error logging, initializes node CPU presence under lock, starts shepherd timing on SMP, and when proc support exists publishes four read only seq views plus the vm sysctl table.

Under SMP the vm sysctls expose a writable interval in jiffies and a restricted refresh trigger with no data store. Under NUMA an additional boolean like control selects NUMA stat visibility bounded between zero and one. Modes make the interval and NUMA control world readable while refresh is root only.

Proc ABI provides buddyinfo and vmstat and zoneinfo as world readable seq files and pagetypeinfo as owner readable only. Debug ABI provides an extfrag directory with unusable index and extfrag index files, both world readable. Sysctl ABI names are stat interval, stat refresh and NUMA stat.

Fragmentation diagnostics iterate all page orders, filling a stack info object per order and printing a fixed point index per order after a node zone header. The unusable metric reports full fragmentation when no free pages exist, otherwise the share of free pages not in suitable blocks scaled to thousandths. The extfrag view skips the memoryless node check that the unusable view performs.
Debug initialization creates a top level extfrag directory and two read only files for unusable and fragmentation indices, returning success unconditionally.

Shadow entry encoding reserves one low bit for working set distinction and derives eviction shifts from word size, radix value bits, node and memcg identifier widths plus swap count for the anonymous variant. Masks are the low bits below those shifts. Bucket order storage is indexed by file versus anonymous and marked read mostly.
Activation filters out uncharged pages when memcg accounting is enabled, then ages nonresident history by the folio size under RCU protection using the folio local reclaim vector.

Shadow node list membership requires the radix tree lock and treats list emptiness as stable under the page cache lock. Nodes that are nonempty and contain only values join the global reclaim list with a node counter increment, while nodes gaining pages or emptying leave the list with a matching decrement, avoiding list lock traffic when already in the desired state.

Shadow shrink pressure is zero when no reclaimable nodes exist or when the count is within a bound derived from present or memcg cache pages shifted by chunk size. The memcg path flushes stats with rate limiting and sums all reclaim list sizes plus reclaimable and unreclaimable slab converted to pages. Excess beyond the bound is reported as the scan target.

Shadow reclaim inverts normal lock order by starting under the list lock, then attempting the page cache lock and optionally the host inode lock with retry on contention. After isolating the object and adjusting the node counter it drops the list lock before validating that the node holds only shadow values and deleting it, accounting a node reclaim event.

Snapshot creation can fail allocation and surfaces a negative memory error pointer instead of an iterator. Negative global counters outside the allowlist only emit warnings without failing refresh. Shadow isolation must cope with lock contention via retry and with unexpected page bearing nodes via one time warnings, since list presence alone does not guarantee purity.
